_strings.@@0d0317558bf9: Treaty conformity — IL conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IL income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IL return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: IL-1040 starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2023 IL-1040 Step 2, Line 1 "Adjusted gross income — Enter the adjusted gross income from your federal return." The instructions ("What is Illinois income?") confirm "Your Illinois income includes the adjusted gross income (AGI) amount figured on your federal return, plus any additional income that must be added to your AGI." Income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI, so it flows through and is not re-taxed. Illinois additions are limited: Line 2 "Federally tax-exempt income" applies ONLY to federally tax-exempt interest and dividend income reported on federal Form 1040 Line 2a (municipal bond interest), not to foreign treaty income; Line 3/Schedule M "Other additions" enumerates specific items (child's 8814 interest/dividends, pass-through additions, Section 529/ABLE earnings, IL-4562 special depreciation, business expense recapture, etc.) and contains no add-back of federal income-tax-treaty-exempt income. There is NO California-style Schedule CA treaty addback. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and IL conforms.
_strings.@@11795485b6fb: 2023 Form IL-1040 Instructions (IL-1040 Instructions R-12/23) — cover/mailing addresses, due date, income tax rate, exemption allowance
_strings.@@18cee8419820: Illinois Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — In general, anyone who qualified for the federal EITC also qualifies for the Illinois EITC. New for tax year 2023, eligibility was expanded (Public Act 102-0700): taxpayers who meet all federal EITC qualifications EXCEPT that they file with an IRS-issued ITIN (no valid SSN required for taxpayer, spouse, or qualifying children), and/or are age 18-24 or 65+ with no qualifying child, may now also claim it. Must have earned income under the federal limits in Table 1, investment income below $11,000, not have filed federal Form 2555, and have been a US resident for at least half of 2023.

_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.

_strings.@@6fb69e391e5c: K-12 Education Expense Credit — Parent or legal guardian of a full-time student who was under age 21 at the close of the school year, where the taxpayer and student were Illinois residents when the expenses were paid, and the student attended kindergarten through 12th grade at a public or nonpublic school in Illinois during 2023. Must complete Section B of Schedule ICR including the K-12 Education Expense Credit Worksheet and attach school receipts.
_strings.@@a344e38434f8: Illinois Property Tax Credit — Illinois residents who, during 2022, owned and lived at a principal residence located in Illinois and paid the Illinois property tax on it during the 2023 tax year. Not available for a vacation home, rental property, vacant lot, farmland, mobile home privilege tax, penalties/fees, or property outside Illinois. Nonresidents may not take this credit. The portion of property tax deductible as a business expense is excluded.
_strings.@@c0779f8e455a: Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit — Created by Public Act 103-0009 for 2023. Available only to a person who received a 2023 Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit Certificate from IDOR. A volunteer emergency worker is a non-full-time member of a fire department, fire protection district, or fire protection association with a Fire Department Identification Number from the Office of the State Fire Marshal. Must have served as a volunteer emergency worker at least 9 months during the taxable year, not receive more than $5,000 in compensation for those services, submit a complete application with IDOR, and be one of the first 10,000 qualified applicants. Note: the income limit that applies to the property tax / K-12 credits does NOT apply to this credit.
_strings.@@ce530ad98232: IL state income tax (2023, flat rate): taxable_base $40,000.00 — which must be the state's own income base derived from federal AGI plus/minus the state's additions and subtractions (NOT raw federal AGI when modifications apply) — with no exemptions or standard deduction to subtract; tax = 0.0495 x $40,000 = $1,98

citation.source: 2023 Form IL-1040 Instructions (IL-1040 Instructions R-12/23) — "The Illinois income tax rate is 4.95 percent (.0495)"; Line 10 exemption allowance ($2,425 per P.A. 103-0009; $4,850 MFJ both; +$1,000 each 65-or-older / blind, Lines 10b/10c); Line 11 net income. Sourcing note: the booklet's own Line 12 instruction reads "Illinois residents: Follow the instructions on the form" — the 4.95% rate and the Line 11 net-income structure are what the booklet states; the Line 12 multiplication is printed on the form itself.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: IL-1040 Line 12 (Tax) = Line 11 (net income = Line 9 base income minus Line 10 exemption allowance) x 4.95% (.0495). Line 9 base income starts from federal AGI (Line 1) plus IL additions (Lines 2-3) minus IL subtractions. Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,000 — Additional $1,000 per 65-or-older checkbox, Line 10b (taxpayer and spouse each). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on the form's Line 10b.); blind ($1,000 — Additional $1,000 per blind checkbox, Line 10c (taxpayer and spouse each). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on the form's Line 10c.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Dependent exemptions (Line 10d, via Schedule IL-E/EIC) are NOT shipped: the per-dependent multiplication was not independently verified — resolve it from the 2023 Schedule IL-E/EIC instructions before claiming dependents; never assume the personal amount applies. Exemption phase-out: the entire Line 10 exemption allowance (including Lines 10b-10d) is $0 when federal AGI exceeds $500,000 (married filing jointly) or $250,000 (all other statuses). Claimed as a dependent by another: if base income exceeds $2,425, the filer's own exemption is $0.
